data.why: the app takes pasted peptide sequences only (no file upload); it ships a built-in example-sequence dropdown (Magainin-2, LL-37 fragment, Indolicidin, synthetic cationic AMP, and a non-AMP control) and its trained XGBoost/RandomForest/LogisticRegression pickles already live under models/, so no data needs to be fetched, trained, or written

goals: paste a candidate peptide sequence and get an AMP vs non-AMP call with a probability and confidence level
see which physicochemical features (charge, hydrophobicity, length, positive-residue fraction) drove the prediction via SHAP
check whether XGBoost, Random Forest, and Logistic Regression agree, to flag borderline sequences for wet-lab follow-up
get a biologically-worded explanation and a lab-assay planning guide (storage, solubility, MIC protocol, hemolysis risk) for the specific sequence
experiment with a mutation-playground slider to see how changing charge/hydrophobicity/length would shift predicted AMP probability
download a CSV feature report for the analyzed sequence

review.summary: The tree captures what the README says the tool is for (predict AMP activity, explain it with SHAP, check three-model agreement, export features) and covers every page and tab, with sound phases and mostly accurate evidence. Before filing, it needs the consensus-threshold wording corrected (votes at 0.40, line at 0.5), the radar overclaim and one wrong citation fixed, and a feature added for the dataset/model-performance pages.
